description: b = a then a[i] = x is visible through b: alloc'd arrays are mutable buffers, unlike Elixir's immutable values. Options: forbid aliasing writable arrays, copy-on-write, or a uniqueness check (Perceus-style refcount == 1). Document the choice in README.

comments.text: Per 'Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?' (defk-dtw.6): Elixir mode is normative, so its result is the expected one. Decide to match Elixir here, or list the difference as a divergence.

Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): aliasing on write is a divergence and must be removed (copy on aliased write, or reject the aliasing at compile time). Arrays mean binaries, writes mean rebinding.
Per defk-dtw.16: until decided, aliasing cases go in the Defk.Divergences registry (defk-63k); done requires it empty.

title: Decide array value semantics (aliasing on write)
